• **Example:** The ride made me feel dizzy.
 
 
 
• **Active** (सक्रिय): Engaging or ready to engage in physically energetic pursuits.
 
 
• **Example:** She leads an active lifestyle, jogging every morning.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She had finished all her homework __from 5 a.m. on that day.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence: **"She had finished all her homework from 5 a.m. on that day,"** is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The preposition "from" is incorrect in this context. The correct preposition is **"by"** to indicate completion before a certain time.
 
• The correct phrase should be "by 5 a.m. on that day," **ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.**
 
• Thus, the error is located in the** preposition** and **the phrase **that follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She had finished all her homework **by 5 a.m. on that day**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "by 5 a.m. in that day" – The preposition "in" is incorrect in this context. It should be "on."
 
• **Option 2:** "No improvement" – This is incorrect as the original sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "till 5 a.m. at that day" – The prepositions "till" and "at" are incorrect in this context. It should be "by" and "on."
